title: Tenant Safepoint Service: jittered reset alignment and auditable quota ledger
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We have recurring incidents and off-by-window billing edge cases when tenant quota reset boundaries overlap DST/timezone boundaries, delayed workers, or when reserved capacity pools migrate. Current "rolling window" resets are implemented as best-effort cron jobs per-region which leads to non-deterministic reset ordering and occasional double-applied resets for tenants with multi-region accounts.

Goal: Implement a Tenant Safepoint Service (TSS) that centralizes the authoritative reset scheduling for tenants, applies jittered safepoints to spread load, records an auditable ledger of applied resets, and exposes an idempotent reset API for worker processes across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. The service should support daily, monthly, and custom rolling windows, and be compatible with reserved capacity carve-outs and burst buckets.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- No more than 0.01% of tenants experience duplicate-reset cases in the next quarter (telemetry-based).
- Resets are idempotent: re-sending the same reset event is a no-op and produces a stable ledger entry.
- Reset schedule supports tenant timezone and a configurable jitter window per tenant class (free/paid/dedicated).
- Audit ledger is queryable by billing and support teams and retains 90 days by default.
- Backfill/reconciliation path documented and runnable for existing tenant reset drift cases.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement billing invoice adjustments or UI; it only provides the operational primitives, APIs, and ledger used by billing jobs and the console.
implementation_plan: 1) Design TSS data model (tenant_id, safepoint_ts, window_type, jitter_nonce, policy_hash, applied_by, ledger_id). 2) Build a small service (stateless API fronted by a consensus-backed storage lease) that returns per-tenant safepoint assignments and accepts confirmations of applied resets. 3) Workers query TSS for their tenant list and scheduled safepoints; on execution they POST confirmation with ledger nonce. 4) TSS guarantees idempotency using (tenant_id, safepoint_ts, policy_hash) as the unique key and writes an append-only ledger row. 5) Add reconciliation job that compares usage ledgers to applied safepoints and emits discrepancy alerts. 6) Integrate with reserved capacity pooling rules so carveouts are applied before ledger insertion. 7) Add telemetry and dashboards.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotent writes and jitter distribution; integration tests simulating delayed workers and duplicate deliveries; a chaos test that randomly delays or drops worker confirmations to ensure reconciliation closes gaps; load test to simulate 200k tenants across regions with jitter spread. E2E: run backfill on a shadow dataset and validate no double-applied resets.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff review: PM and Billing ops approved scope; two open questions about ledger retention and customer-facing adjustments. Action: set default retention to 90 days and route invoice adjustments to Billing-ops backlog.

2026-03-04 - Design review: chose idempotency key = (tenant_id, safepoint_ts, policy_hash). Engineering suggested adding jitter_nonce to avoid coordinator hot-spots; accepted. Marisol to prototype storage schema using CockroachDB append-only table.

2026-03-06 - Prototype complete: safepoint assignment endpoint returns jittered timestamp and policy_hash. Found race condition when two workers for same tenant request assignment simultaneously; resolved via DB unique constraint and retry with exponential backoff. PR opened.

2026-03-08 - Security review triage: security asked for KMS-protected signing of ledger rows to prevent tampering in private deployments. Decided to make signing optional via config flag; follow-up ticket for integration with HSM/KMS in private installs. Marked security_review_required=false for this ticket (signing follow-up will be flagged).

2026-03-10 - QA: ran chaos test that dropped 10% of confirmation events; reconciliation job detected 98% of gaps and auto-closed 75% after re-triggering workers. Remaining cases require manual billing ops review; added to runbook.
